bullets.title: CRWV: Strong Q3 beat/raise; PT raised, financing concerns addressed
bullets.body: CoreWeave surged ~13-15% premarket after a strong Q3 beat/raise: capacity sold out through 2027, $9B in customer pre-payments expected in next 3 months, and >75% of 2027 capex fundable from backlog. Citi raised PT to $149 (from $128); MS highlighted CRWV +15% as AI capex beneficiary. DADCO maintains Neutral, flagging ~3% returns vs ~10% cost of capital and 35M share ATM plus heavy insider selling as ongoing concerns. UBS Buy but cautious given ORCL's similar post-earnings fade pattern.

bullets.title: NVDA: Removed as Top Pick at MS; positioning most bearish since '23; political risk emerging
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley removed NVDA as a Top Pick following a -25% decline since Oct 2, though GB200/300 rack shipments were +16% m/m in October with 2027 forecast of 90.4K racks. Citi flags NVDA net crowding at lowest level since 2023, implied earnings move of +/-7.7% (highest since Feb 2025), and 25-delta put-call skew at 89th percentile. Separately, Republican Senator Cramer called for CEO Huang's resignation, potentially weakening NVDA's lobbying position on the Chip Security Act.

bullets.title: AAPL: China Renaissance upgrades to Buy, PT $425 (22% upside)
bullets.body: China Renaissance Securities (US) upgraded Apple to Buy from Hold with a $425 price target, implying ~22% upside from $348.51. This compares to FactSet consensus target of $341.38 (range $250–$405).

bullets.title: Semis broadly: Notebook ODM data weak; KeyBanc cuts outlook for AMD, INTC, MU, NVDA
bullets.body: October PC notebook shipments came in at 10.7M units, -22% m/m and -23% y/y, missing the 11.5M estimate. KeyBanc lowered full-year 2026 notebook shipment outlook to -12-15% y/y (from -10-15%) and projects another -8-12% decline in 2027, negatively flagging AMD, INTC, MU, and NVDA exposure to this end market.

bullets.title: TLN: 750 MW capacity deal at ~$365/MW-day generates ~$100M annually, de-risks production
bullets.body: Talen Energy signed a 750 MW long-term PJM capacity agreement (2029-2036) at approximately $365/MW-day, generating roughly $100M in annual revenue and de-risking the production profile. Stock was up ~6.3% in pre-market. Both Morgan Stanley and Oppenheimer flagged the deal as constructive, with MS noting the price is above cap.

bullets.title: VRT: T12M orders imply $30B+ N12M revenue vs. consensus $18.4B — ~60% upside signal
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley highlighted that Vertiv's trailing-12-month orders imply a next-12-month revenue opportunity of $30B+, versus Street consensus of $18.4B, signaling roughly 60% upside. JPM moved VRT to Neutral from NR, lowering AI-linked price targets amid broader industrials caution.

bullets.title: AT&T (T): JPM OW, $31 PT; SpaceX spectrum filing pressures legacy telecoms
bullets.body: JPM maintains T at Overweight with a $31 PT following a management meeting covering SpaceX, D2D, fiber, FWA, and spectrum. The FCC accepted Starlink's application to transfer control of 800 MHz SMRS licenses (~$8B deal); JPMorgan argues telecom sentiment will be hit by potential fourth-entrant risk, though UBS notes the selloff seems overdone given time needed to scale.

bullets.title: ADBE: Citi maintains Sell; incoming CEO's short-contract strategy risks ARR downside
bullets.body: Citi reiterates Sell on Adobe, noting the incoming CEO's emphasis on shorter-duration contracts and lower initial monetization, which is expected to create downside risk to ARR. ADBE trades at 16x EV/Sales 2027 despite an 80% YTD gain, with elevated expectations already priced in.

bullets.title: CSCO: MS Equal-weight, $120 PT; FY28 gross margin compression the key risk
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley maintains Equal-weight on Cisco at $120, cautioning that gross margin pressure is concentrated in FY28 as hyperscaler mix grows — Street models ~147bps GM decline in FY27 and ~146bps in FY28. Near-term FQ1 print expected to be better driven by an upcoming price increase (~$18.3-18.4B revenue, ~$1.36-$1.38 EPS), with AI revenue target expected to be raised to $8B. Valuation at ~18x FY28 P/E seen as offering limited upside.

bullets.title: TTWO: Catalyst-driven long into GTA VI launch (11/19); Q2 bookings below guide
bullets.body: Hedgeye frames Take-Two as a catalyst-driven long into the November 19 GTA VI launch. Q2 net bookings came in at $1,601.3M (-18.3% YoY), $18.7M below the guide floor due to NBA 2K weakness, but the GTA VI date has been held through prior guidance, keeping the near-term setup intact.

bullets.title: ABNB gaining OTA share; EXPE faces mounting North America B2C risk
bullets.body: Hedgeye notes Airbnb's regional growth has more than doubled peers in the US, with notable share gains, while risks are mounting for Expedia in core North American B2C room nights.

bullets.title: HLT/MAR: RevPAR tracking well ahead of consensus for 4Q26
bullets.body: US RevPAR rose +4.7% Y/Y for the week ending 11/7/26. 4Q26 is tracking +7.8% overall. HLT is running at +7.3% weighted RevPAR vs. consensus +4.5%, and MAR at +7.0% vs. consensus +5.9%, with five of seven remaining 2026 weeks featuring easy comps from prior-year negatives.

bullets.title: RCL: Citi Buy; Europe demand, onboard spend key 2027 tailwinds despite 1H structural drag
bullets.body: Citi reiterates Buy on Royal Caribbean, flagging Europe as the largest incremental 2027 tailwind alongside record onboard spending and new-ship premiums. Nearly 100bps of full-year structural yield headwinds are concentrated in 1H27 from dry docks and accounting timing. Sandals viewed as a customer-acquisition platform with margin upside potential.

bullets.title: WBD: JPM Underweight, $9 PT; content licensing miss, FCF guidance disappoints
bullets.body: JPMorgan maintains Underweight on Warner Bros. Discovery at $9. Q3 revenue/AOI of $566M/$70M missed estimates of $575M/$88M; content licensing of $84M fell short of $100M estimate due to Netflix Walking Dead agreement timing. FY26 FCF guidance remains ~$150M but JPM estimates $140M conservatively. Domestic affiliate revenue declined 10.8% Y/Y.

bullets.title: NFLX/TKO/LYV: Live entertainment framed as AI hedge; streaming ad revenue increasingly critical
bullets.body: Ari Emanuel (via Blackstone) argues live sports and events cannot be displaced by AI, making them structurally more valuable as digital content commoditizes. Streaming advertising is increasingly critical to Netflix economics as content supply expands. AI is expected to lower production costs but human judgment remains essential to premium content creation.

bullets.title: SHOP/CLS: Pre-market movers in Canadian session on broad tech rally
bullets.body: Shopify rose +1.2% (C$210.70) and Celestica surged +6.4% (C$339.25) in mid-morning Canadian trading, with CLS likely benefiting from the broader AI infrastructure sympathy rally following CRWV's strong print.

bullets.title: GOOGL/AMZN/MSFT: Hyperscalers preferred over semis/software on contracted AI capacity
bullets.body: Militia Capital's David Orr prefers hyperscalers (Alphabet, Amazon, Microsoft) over AI infrastructure plays, citing contracted capacity supporting ~35% returns on capital. AWS CEO expects capacity constraints to persist 2+ years, targeting $1T annual revenue in 5-10 years; AWS inference is currently <1% of eventual market. MS identifies Microsoft as its preferred AI infrastructure play post-midterms.

bullets.title: HD/LOW: Ace Hardware Q3 comp acceleration to +2.0% a positive read-through ahead of earnings
bullets.body: Mizuho flags Ace Hardware's Q3 comps of +2.0% (up from +1.1% in Q2) as a positive leading indicator for Home Depot and Lowe's earnings next week, given >90% historical correlation since late 2018. HD Street estimates embed domestic comps of +1.5%, with Mizuho seeing potential market share pickup; LOW consensus is +0.4% vs. Mizuho's flattish forecast.

bullets.title: GLW: Jefferies initiates Buy on persistent fiber shortage and $18B+ hyperscaler agreements
bullets.body: Jefferies initiated Corning at Buy, citing a persistent fiber shortage, over $18B in hyperscaler supply agreements, and rising optical intensity in AI data centers. The initiation is part of a broader semi-cap equipment coverage launch that also includes TER at Buy on NVDA/hyperscaler dual-sourcing driving SoC share gains.

bullets.title: PYPL: German antitrust probe into fee restrictions for online merchants
bullets.body: Germany's Federal Cartel Office indicated PayPal's fee restrictions for online merchants may violate German antitrust law, adding a regulatory overhang to the name.
